references.text: The same promise that no one shall be barren in Israel, including both people and livestock
Abraham died 'old and full of days', an example of the fulfillment of the promise of full life spans
Isaac died 'old and full of days', another example of God's promise to fill the days of life
The promise of reaching old age at death, like a sheaf gathered in its season
Sarah was barren, but God opened her womb - the opposite of the curse mentioned here
God opened Leah's womb, demonstrating his power over barrenness
God remembered Rachel and opened her womb after her period of barrenness
God lets the barren woman dwell in a house as a joyful mother of children
The promise to satisfy with long life and show salvation
A prophetic promise of long life in the coming kingdom
Both passages highlight the theme of 'full days' and God's protection of lifespan, contrasting with human frailty.
